title: Visa - Interchange fee complexity fueled a $5.54B merchant antitrust settlement
clean_text: Merchants and trade associations sued Visa, Mastercard, and card-issuing banks in 2005 over alleged price-fixing and anticompetitive practices in interchange fee setting; a 2019 settlement totaled $5.54 billion, affirmed on appeal in 2023, with claims covering transactions from 2004-2019 and a claims period extended to February 2025. Separately, in recent years dozens of large merchants including Amtrak, Crate & Barrel, Dick's Sporting Goods, and Nike settled individual interchange fee claims against Visa and Mastercard, and a UK tribunal ruled that Visa and Mastercard's default multilateral interchange fees breached competition law. Merchants commonly cite interchange fee complexity -- which varies by merchant category code, transaction type, and risk level -- as difficult to predict and budget against.
